name: Mono-compatible chord-split hard L/R pad width
goal: Widen a pad without chorus/spreader phase smear: duplicate the synth+MIDI, mute alternating chord tones on each copy (interleaved split), hard-pan L vs R so channels play different notes of the same harmony—yielding extreme width with healthier correlation than chorus/stereo-spread FX.

source.title: How to make true mono compatible stereo widening to your synth sounds #kyaalmix

prerequisites: DAW that can duplicate instrument+MIDI; pad synth with multi-note chords

inputs.name: chord_midi
inputs.description: Pad chord progression to split across two layers

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Ableton/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Goal is different L vs R note content—not delayed/frequency-split copies of the same notes.

steps.action: Start from a basic pad chord patch. Note that chorus widens but can sound phasy/warbly; frequency stereo-spread often fails to feel truly wide and can sound inside-out.
Duplicate the synth instance with identical settings and copy the MIDI to both tracks.
On track A piano roll, mute every other note top→bottom; on track B mute the complementary set bottom→top so together they reconstruct the full chords but separately play different notes.
Hard-pan A fully left and B fully right; play together for maximum width.
Check a correlation/phase meter: split technique should sit near ~0 (very wide) without deep negative swings; compare vs chorus (often flangy + negative correlation) and spreader (weaker width).
steps.expect: Wide image, healthier correlation than chorus

verification: Alone, each layer is incomplete chords; together they form full harmony
Hard L/R pan yields strong width
Correlation stays healthier than chorus comparison
